newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: IMF tells Zambia to get budget back on track.
newsitem.headline: IMF tells Zambia to get budget back on track.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday that Zambia would have to put its budget back on track before discussions on the country's second-year Enhanced Structral Adjustment Facility could resume.
IMF area representaive Elwaleed Taha said the government had also agreed to initiate civil service reform before the second-year ESAF was negotiated.
"The Zambian government and the IMF mission agreed on a work programme to facilitate the resumption of discussions on a second-year ESAF in the near future," Taha told Reuters in an interview.
"Areas of agreement included initiation of work on civil service reform and securing attainment of a government target of a budget surplus of one percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP)," he added.
The government failed to achieve a budget surplus in the first quarter of the year as projected in the 1997 budget.
"The government agreed that some work needs to be done on the budget. It also agreed to initiate civil service reform this year," Taha said.
He said negotiations on the second-year ESAF would depend on how quickly the government addressed the IMF concerns.
In February the IMF endorsed the country's performance under the first ESAF year and released SDR 10 million (about $14 million) to the country.
Under an agreement reached last year, the IMF endorsement means that Paris Club members will reschedule 67 percent of Zambia's debts to them.
Zambia has a total external debt of around $6.38 billion.

Key achievements leading to the IMF endorsement of Zambia's performance under the first ESAF year included the reduction of inflation to the lowest annual level in eight years at 35 percent, a budget surplus of one percent of GDP and a 6.5 percent economic growth in 1996.
Other achievements included an increase in social sector spending at 34.5 percent, and progress in the privatisation of state-run enterprises.
Zambia regained its eligibility to use IMF financial resources in December 1995 after clearing arrears to the IMF of SDR 830.2 million.
The government, meanwhile, is trying to restore normal relations with bilateral donors who cut aid over governance concerns last year.
One third of the country's $1.1 billion budget for 1997 is dependant on donor aid.
